patterns.title: Declaration and definition chronology can change GC/1.3.2 output
patterns.summary: Moving file-scope definitions earlier can change one-pass visibility, register allocation, section extents, and relocations even when the C declarations appear equivalent. MDBank pass2 proves the inverse extraction case: when authenticated source chronology makes a helper body visible to a selected caller but the helper must remain fallback-owned, an ordinary local `static inline` copy can preserve the original auto-inline expansion without emitting a second helper symbol or using force-inline controls.
patterns.conditions: Apply as a compiler-wide diagnostic under GC/1.3.2; probe each owner locally because stage.c is a counterexample to the mdparty tail-definition requirement.

source_condition.change: Move file-scope object definitions earlier or otherwise alter declaration/definition chronology while retaining nominally equivalent declarations.

same symbol ownership and types
before/after object and relocation comparison
target proof that the helper expansion is present while a duplicate helper csect and call relocation are absent

register allocation
.text size
.bss size
relocation addends or object chronology
whether a nested helper operation remains a call when the enclosing helper is later auto-inlined
known_signatures: a semantics-preserving reorder regresses many exact functions
section extent changes without an intentional data-layout change
a standalone helper compiled with prototype-only visibility remains call-bearing inside a later exact auto-inline expansion
complete copied bodies and absent call relocations prove a depth-two inline chain whose result changes when one definition moves
an isolated caller becomes exact with an authenticated local static-inline helper while the generated object emits no second helper csect

patterns.rule: Treat declaration chronology as a testable compiler variable; do not modernize definition placement or copy a tail-definition layout without owner-local proof. During extraction, a fallback-owned helper may be represented by an authenticated ordinary local static-inline body only when target instructions prove the expansion, target relocations prove the missing call, generated sections prove no duplicate helper emission, and all fallback and direct consumers remain exact.
safe_actions: make a bounded owner-local chronology probe
compare every independently exact function and affected data section
record both positive and negative owner results
for a source-extracted caller, compare a normal static-inline local helper under the pinned auto-inline command before considering any compiler control

MDBank pass2 recovered four isolated chronology relations (fn_1_AC4 to fn_1_1200, fn_1_3100 to fn_1_3164, fn_1_111B0 to fn_1_111F8, and fn_1_1161C to fn_1_11678) with ordinary authenticated static-inline helper copies under the normal GC/1.3.2 auto-inline command. Ten text-only owners retained 12/12 functions, 2,780 text bytes, and 141 physical relocations; no source-only helper csect was emitted and the retail REL remained exact.

MDSing pass31 recovered fn_1_EA7C and fn_1_F15C with an authenticated depth-two static-inline selection updater. Specializing its fixed 5.0f donor interpolation to target-owned 4.0f/5.0f constants preserved MWCC constant folding with no helper csect, while fn_1_E688 remained the exact expanded body in the chain.
mdbankdll fn_1_281C compiled exactly before fn_1_11900 was defined; later fn_1_28B4 expanded fn_1_281C but preserved the nested fn_1_11900 call relocation
mode-select wave 68 proved several standalone-plus-expanded and depth-two helper relations from complete instruction copies and absent call relocations

Ending pass4 bound a target-address-ordered lifecycle leaf set even where authenticated historical source placed neighboring definitions in a different order; nine text-only owners remained 12/12 exact, so source definition chronology and retail split order were treated as separate evidenced variables

patterns.title: Mine cross-owner analogues by ordered relocation skeleton, then rebind target ownership
patterns.summary: Sixty-four eligible REL target functions totaling 15,908 text bytes and 1,081 physical relocations became independently exact across mdsingdll and endingdll when candidates were selected by ordered calls, control shape, and relocations, then rebound to target-owned symbols and types and verified as consumed generated objects through the retail REL. Authenticated donor helper bodies can restore target auto-inline closure at zero source-only helper text when target call relocations prove the helper was not emitted. Authenticated historical C is source-shape evidence rather than function-boundary authority: target symbol extents, relocations, and multiple independent donor fingerprints delimit any adjacent historical tail. Exact perimeter functions remain independently valuable when an interior analogue is blocked by inline chronology, scheduling, or compiler-owned conversion pools. A fast Gekko-aware decoder such as powerpc-rs can increase discovery throughput by fingerprinting opcode, branch, and relocation skeletons in bulk, but its output remains ranking evidence rather than ownership or exactness proof.

patterns.rule: Treat cross-owner same-game source as a ranked hypothesis generator: use a Gekko-aware decoder such as powerpc-rs to fingerprint ordered opcodes, branches, relocations, and control shape at catalog scale; cluster compatible targets; then rebind every contract from target evidence and retain only subsets with exact instructions, relocations, generated-object consumption, consumers, and retail replay. Decoder similarity is never ownership proof, and historical source adjacency is never target function-boundary proof. When a target caller lacks a helper-call relocation, an authenticated donor helper may be reconstructed as a natural static inline above the caller only if the target object emits no source-only helper text and target-owned data bindings remain exact. After bounded probes, keep dependency-closed exact perimeter functions and revert pool-, scheduling-, inline-, or boundary-blocked interiors instead of discarding the whole cluster.

patterns.title: Triangulate configured extent and public consumers before retaining an opaque overlay
patterns.summary: Independent staffdll, mdbankdll, mdpresultdll, and main-board recoveries replaced misleading offset-only, first-word, incomplete-prefix, or opaque byte interpretations with natural aggregates after configured sizes, complete element strides, public field types, callbacks, and state consumers were triangulated; w01 cleanup additionally proved that ordinary ABI alignment must supply narrow-to-wide member gaps instead of manually named padding. Exact text and relocations were preserved across both compiler profiles.

source_condition.change: Choose a natural aggregate owner and typed field chain, relying on ordinary ABI alignment before retaining an offset-only overlay, first-word pointer interpretation, or manual padding member.

typed offsets and strides from public or authenticated owner contracts
multiple independent read, write, callback, teardown, or state consumers
exact instructions, relocations, and retained consumers

configured size divided by repeated consumer count yields a stable natural element stride
an indexed SDK global emits the wrong multiply or displacement when only an element prefix is declared

patterns.title: Result signedness of an integer call decides xoris float conversion and cmplwi/cmpwi
patterns.summary: When a call result feeds a float context, MWCC emits the signed conversion (xoris 0x8000 with the 4330000080000000 magic) only if the result type is signed; an unsigned result emits no xoris with the 4330000000000000 magic. the exact build profile of the consuming TU

patterns.title: MWCC .rodata is a single region in strict creation order, not named objects then a literal pool
patterns.summary: At -O0 the object's .rodata is one region emitted in strict creation order. Named const objects and pooled literals interleave freely; there is no named-objects-first region and no dedup between a named object and an equal pool literal, though pool literals do dedup against each other. What differs between constructs is only WHEN a constant is created: a named object at its definition point (whether or not anything references it), an expression literal at the codegen of the referencing function, a static inline body's constants at its FIRST EXPANSION, and an extern-inline function-local static under '#pragma cplusplus on' at PARSE of the inline body even when never called. Only an uncalled static inline emits nothing.
patterns.conditions: Apply when a target and candidate hold the same .rodata contents in a different order, or when choosing a construct to place constants ahead of the first function's codegen.

no emission at all for an uncalled static inline, with or without a function-scope static const

patterns.summary: MEASURED: pool references are relocations against a symbol with the instruction immediate left at zero, so permuting .rodata cannot change any .text byte. SEPARATELY, and carried from an unpushed campaign branch rather than measured here: objdiff's .rodata percentage is not a gate, and the criterion offered instead is an identical common prefix plus the direction of the size difference, because dtk's split rounds sections up with trailing zeros. The mechanism behind that second half is independently supported by the card dtk-synthetic-gap-not-source-ownership; the specific object counts and percentages are not.

patterns.title: Parentheses, register, const and compound assignment are -O0 no-ops; only real regrouping moves temporaries
patterns.summary: Under the measured GC/2.7 -O0 controls, redundant parentheses, the register storage class, const on parameters and locals, and compound assignment are codegen no-ops, and so are declared-but-never-referenced locals. Float temporaries are numbered by expression-tree shape rather than liveness, so only a genuine operator or tree-shape change moves code generation. Equality-operand reversal was also measured neutral in two GC/2.6 board/audio campaigns. A helper's definition position and an arithmetic rewrite such as division to reciprocal multiplication are NOT cosmetic forms.
patterns.conditions: Apply before spending a search budget on cosmetic source variations, or when a same-operand different-destination-register difference needs explaining.

source_condition.change: Add or remove parentheses, register/const qualifiers, compound-assignment forms, equality-operand order, or an arithmetic regrouping/rewrite.
requires: byte comparison of the two candidate objects, not a match percentage
an instruction-stream alignment that separates structural from operand differences
the exact build profile of the owning TU

possible_changes: no change at all for parentheses, register, const, or compound assignment
no change at all for a declared-but-never-referenced local
no change in the measured GC/2.6 board/audio comparisons after reversing equality operands
a different destination register when the expression tree's depth changes
the same destinations with swapped fmuls A/C operand fields when a commutative operand pair is reversed
different load or operand order when division by 2 is rewritten as multiplication by 0.5
known_signatures: probes p5a/p5b differ by redundant parentheses, register on a parameter and two locals, const on all parameters, and += versus = ... + : .text 60 bytes on both sides and byte-identical
probes p7a/p7c differ only by redundant parentheses: byte-identical at 16 bytes
probes p7a/p7b, (a*b)*(c*d) versus ((a*b)*c)*d: same 16 bytes, different destinations - p7a fmuls f5,f1,f2 / f0,f3,f4 / f1,f5,f0 against p7b fmuls f0,f1,f2 / f0,f3,f0 / f1,f4,f0
a balanced tree needs a second live temporary where a left-leaning tree reuses f0
probes p7a/p7d, (a*b)*(c*d) versus (b*a)*(d*c): destinations IDENTICAL (f5, f0, f1), only the leaf operand fields swap - p7d fmuls f5,f2,f1 / f0,f4,f3 / f1,f5,f0
probes p12a/p12b differ by two unused float locals: byte-identical at .text 36 bytes with no .rodata
waves 18 and 26 reversed equality operands in board/audio but MWCC retained the same cmplw operand order
waves 49 and 68 independently show division by 2.0 versus multiplication by 0.5 changing target operand or load order

patterns.rule: Under the exact measured profile, do not repeat bounded-neutral probes for parentheses, register, const, compound assignment, leftover unused locals, or the board/audio equality reversal. When a destination register is wrong with correct operands, test one target-backed operator or expression-tree shape, not punctuation. A helper's file position and `/ 2` versus `* 0.5` are real code-generation changes and are outside the neutral set.
safe_actions: compare candidate objects byte-for-byte rather than by match percentage
drive structural insert/delete differences to zero before reading operand differences
record eliminated axes so the next agent does not repeat them
preserve the target-authenticated arithmetic operator instead of normalizing division into reciprocal multiplication
re-measure before carrying any neutral-form result to another compiler profile
examples: probes p5a/p5b: four cosmetic axes changed at once (parentheses, register, const, compound assignment) still produce byte-identical .text
probes p12a/p12b: two never-referenced float locals cost nothing, so a leftover declaration need not be deleted to match
waves 18 and 26: swapping the equality operands in mbMusBoardPlay and MusBoardFade was byte-neutral and did not reverse the emitted cmplw
counterexamples: REFUTED by measurement: 'a helper's definition position is an -O0 no-op'. Probes p8a/p8b differ only in whether the static helper is defined above the caller or below it behind a prototype: .text 148 bytes against 112, AND .rodata order reversed, because -inline auto expands the helper only when it is already visible. Helper position is a real lever - see gc26-o0-definition-order-and-call-evaluation and mwcc-o0-inline-expansion-frame-allocation.

NOT a sweep axis: commuting a commutative pair does change bytes, but not the way an earlier revision of this card claimed. Probes p7a/p7d show destination registers UNCHANGED (f5, f0, f1) with only the fmuls A/C operand fields swapping - it reallocates nothing. The bounded protocol in mwcc-commutative-fmuls-source-swap-canonicalizes-neutral governs: run ONE direct reversal for an isolated operand-order mismatch, record the result, and stop. Do not sweep.
NOT neutral: wave 49 LogAdd became exact only with natural difference / 2.0 instead of difference * 0.5, and wave 68 independently observed the same load-order distinction for fn_1_8EC8.
NOT a universal rewrite: wave 54's signed timeout / 2 probe emitted extra signed rounding and extension code and was reverted.

Scalar locals are enregistered per live-range web; the register keyword does not decide which local wins a callee-saved register. Carried from the campaign, not isolated by these probes - p5a/p5b only show that adding register changes nothing.
Neutrality here is about .text. It says nothing about .rodata order, which follows creation order - see mwcc-rodata-is-one-region-in-creation-order.

patterns.title: When only stack-slot numbers remain, the lever is an inline expansion, not a nested block
patterns.summary: A bounded diagnostic for a function whose instructions are all correct but whose r1 displacements are wrong. Locals are slotted in declaration order, descending, with compiler temporaries interleaved at their point of use. An inline expansion instead allocates the inlinee's locals or return temporary from the bottom of the caller frame. GC/2.6 now confirms the return-value boundary directly: a visible zero-argument scalar getter creates the target low-frame store/load temporary, while assigning that getter directly to the final destination avoids the extra caller-local store/load bridge. Declaration order inside a helper remains load-bearing when declarations are independent, and the helper must be defined above its caller for automatic expansion.
patterns.conditions: Apply only when structural insert/delete differences are already zero and every remaining difference is a stack-slot number or an inlinee register assignment.

source_condition.change: Extract repeated code into a static inline helper, reorder an inline helper's locals, change how a caller value reaches the inlinee, or replace a caller intermediate with a direct assignment from a visible scalar getter.
requires: structural differences already driven to zero
every r1 displacement dumped from both instruction streams and diffed
the inlinee's own declaration order treated as significant
byte comparison of the candidate object, not a match percentage

possible_changes: a whole group of stack slots moving together to the bottom of the frame
changed register or slot assignment inside the expansion from reordering the helper's locals
extra stores at expansion entry, and a shifted frame, when a value is passed by value
a two-level local group when one helper's call is nested inside another
one low-frame store/load return temporary per expanded scalar getter, without a caller-local copy bridge when the result is assigned directly
known_signatures: probes p6d/p6e differ only in the declaration order of the helper's two INDEPENDENT locals: .text 152 bytes on both sides but three allocation fields differ, f28 and f29 exchanged (fmuls f28,f31,f30 -> f29,f31,f30; fadds f29,f0,f30 -> f28,f0,f30; fmuls f27,f28,f29 -> f27,f29,f28)

probes p6a/p6b are the boundary case: when the helper's second local DEPENDS on the first, exchanging the declarations is byte-identical at 140 bytes, so this lever only bites on independent declarations
probes p6a/p6c: by-pointer 140 bytes against by-value-plus-out-pointer 164 bytes; p6c also adds a term, so 24 bytes is an upper bound on the by-value cost rather than an isolated measurement
probes p8a/p8b: a helper defined above the caller is auto-expanded (.text 148) while the same helper defined below behind a prototype is called (.text 112), and .rodata order reverses with it

CAMPAIGN, NOT REPRODUCIBLE HERE (branch codex/w01dll-match 7d0876c9 is unpushed; needs a full build): w01Dll fn_1_13CC stalled at struct=0 with 46 differences that were all stack-slot numbers, the target holding inner-loop locals at 0x008-0x018 and inlined-sqrtf temporaries at 0x068/0x06c while ours was inverted; extracting two numeric helpers, one nested inside the other, moved all 30 float slots into agreement at once. Treat as unverified.

GC/2.6 main:board/telop mbTelopTimeChangeCreate: direct scalar locals were exact-sized at 2432 bytes but left 137 argument/slot differences; two visible zero-argument getters plus direct destination assignment produced the target low-frame slots and a strict 2432/2432-byte, zero-difference function. Keeping caller intermediates with the same getters instead emitted 2448 bytes and four inserted bridge instructions.

patterns.rule: Once structural differences are zero and only slot numbers remain, reach for a static inline helper rather than a nested block and define it above its caller so -inline auto can expand it. If the target shows a field load followed by a low-frame store/load before the final assignment or arithmetic, test a zero-argument scalar getter and assign its result directly; do not preserve a caller intermediate that adds a second store/load bridge. Pass caller-frame values by pointer for multi-output helpers, and treat independent declaration order as part of the helper's identity.
safe_actions: dump and diff every r1 displacement from both streams before editing
extract repeats as static inline helpers taking parameters rather than copying arguments into locals
nest one helper call inside another to reproduce a two-level local group
pass a value the caller must keep by pointer, which MWCC folds into an r1 displacement at no instruction cost
for a single scalar result, compare direct assignment from a visible getter against exactly one caller-intermediate control
examples: probes p6d/p6e: exchanging two independent declarations inside the helper moves three allocation fields at identical size, so the helper's declaration order is part of its identity
probes p8a/p8b: the same helper is expanded or called purely on whether its definition precedes the caller

CAMPAIGN, NOT REPRODUCIBLE HERE: w01Dll fn_1_13CC closed on this lever after 361 declaration-order permutations and 719 inner-block permutations had failed, and passing one value by pointer put it at frame offset 0xa8 with two other locals pushed down. Treat as unverified.

main:board/telop mbTelopTimeChangeCreate uses two visible scalar getters assigned directly to starNum and the subtraction expression; their expanded return temporaries land at r1+0x24 and r1+0x20 and the function is strict-exact at 2432 bytes.
counterexamples: The lever does not always bite: probes p6a/p6b exchange the helper's two declarations and emit byte-identical code, because the second local depends on the first. Only INDEPENDENT declarations reorder the allocation, so a null result here does not refute the inline hypothesis.
Defining the helper below its caller silently removes the lever entirely - it is then a real call, not an expansion (probes p8a/p8b). Check visibility before concluding the helper shape is wrong.
Passing the value by value instead of by pointer adds work at expansion entry and shifts the frame (probes p6a/p6c, 140 against 164 bytes).

For scalar getters, assigning through a caller intermediate is not neutral: the mbTelopTimeChangeCreate control grew from the target 2432 bytes to 2448 bytes by adding a second store/load bridge for each getter result.

CAMPAIGN, NOT REPRODUCIBLE HERE: plain nested blocks were reported unable to produce the layout - a nested block's locals continue the enclosing block's descending run - and nesting made w01Dll worse in every ordering tried (46 -> 49..81). Treat as unverified.
The ascending-from-frame-bottom direction is carried from the w01Dll campaign and was not re-measured in the small probes here, where the inlinee's locals were enregistered rather than stack-homed.

patterns.title: Keep compound assignments inside the consuming condition when the target reuses the updated value
patterns.summary: Across MWCC O0 profiles, a compound or result assignment written inside its consuming condition can keep the produced value live through the store and comparison; separating the assignment may add a reload, grow the function, or rotate saved registers.
patterns.conditions: Use when target instructions store an updated or returned value and immediately compare that same value, while an otherwise natural separated assignment differs only by a reload, size change, or register-lifetime cycle.

source_condition.change: Restore one target-backed compound/result assignment to the condition that immediately consumes it.
requires: identical source semantics for the combined and separated forms
target instruction order proving immediate store and comparison
one bounded separated-versus-combined compiler control
exact relocations and no regression of exact owner neighbors

possible_changes: reuse of the updated FPR across a store and comparison
removal of a redundant reload
shorter function text
collapse of a saved-register lifetime cycle around an assigned call result
known_signatures: separated `x += step; if (x > limit)` reloads x while `(x += step) > limit` compares the produced value
the separated float form is four bytes larger than the target
an assigned call result written inside `if` removes a multi-register color cycle without changing calls or relocations
matching sibling functions repeat the compound-assignment condition naturally

patterns.rule: Test the natural assignment-consuming condition as one bounded source-shape variable when target order proves the lifetime; retain it only with exact text, relocations, and consumers, and never replace unrelated control flow with comma expressions or assignment side effects solely to shape registers.
safe_actions: compare separated and compound forms once under the exact compiler profile
verify the target store precedes the immediate comparison
look for exact same-owner or same-game compound-assignment siblings
preserve ordinary separated statements when the target reloads or the condition is not the immediate consumer
examples: endingdll fn_1_193C: `(work->time += step) > duration` is strict exact at 484 bytes; the separated form is 488 bytes and reloads the float
mdpartydll fn_1_5324, fn_1_6324, and fn_1_737C repeat exact compound float-update conditions under the GC/1.3.2 owner profile
mdpartydll fn_1_3BEA8 keeps an assigned call result inside the consuming equality and removes a three-way saved-register cycle
counterexamples: A semantically equivalent assignment form is not evidence unless the target store/compare or result lifetime agrees.
Do not introduce comma expressions, duplicate side effects, or assignment conditions solely to force registers.
Folded assignment conditions that are byte-neutral or worse should be reverted and recorded as negative evidence.

patterns.title: Use natural local declaration order and first use to resolve saved-register cycles
patterns.summary: Across MWCC O0 profiles, adjacent same-width or pointer locals can receive different saved registers when their natural declaration order, initialization point, first semantic use, or static use count changes, even when control flow, types, size, and relocations are otherwise identical. Under the measured GC/2.6 -O0,p path, source FPR locals are assigned before PCode graph coloring: allocate_local_FPRs repeatedly selects the highest VarInfo.usage value, resolves ties by local-list traversal, and assigns descending nonvolatile FPRs. Graph coloring then handles compiler temporaries. A native Win32 Debug API probe in tools/mwcc_win32_varinfo.py can pause the pinned compiler at allocate_local_FPRs and read named VarInfo usage and assignments; this is diagnostic only and does not establish source names or source authority. A pure cycle is therefore evidence of an earlier source-local ranking or AST difference, not authority to force a register.
patterns.conditions: Use only for an exact-sized function whose remaining differences form a small same-width saved-register cycle after structural control flow, owner types, calls, and relocations already agree.

source_condition.change: Restore the target-backed declaration order, initialization point, and first semantic use of adjacent natural locals.
requires: authenticated local types and ownership
exact function size and structural instruction sequence
a bounded declaration-order, initialization-point, or first-use control
exact relocations and zero regression of exact owner neighbors

possible_changes: rotation of callee-saved GPR assignments
a later saved-register lifetime when declaration and assignment are separated naturally
operand-field changes without instruction insertion or deletion
unchanged frame size, calls, and relocation stream
no emitted change when first-use chronology dominates the declarations
known_signatures: two pointer locals exchange r30 and r31 after one natural declaration-order swap
sequential same-type loop locals occupy descending saved registers in declaration/first-use order
an exact-sized function retains only a two- or three-register ARG cycle
a declaration initializer begins an owner-pointer lifetime before a target cleanup call cluster
legal scope or declaration movement is byte-neutral when it does not change first use
two exact-sized functions close after declaration-order changes remove complete inverse four- and eight-operand saved-register cycles
a GC/2.6 -O0,p FPR cycle follows descending source-local VarInfo.usage before temporary graph coloring
the native Win32 probe pauses at allocate_local_FPRs and reports named-local usage before the compiler assigns descending nonvolatile FPRs

patterns.rule: Test one natural adjacent-local declaration order, one target-backed initialization point, and one independently justified first-use chronology when the mismatch is a pure saved-register cycle. Treat those as separate variables. Retain the form only when typed semantics, complete text, relocations, and consumers are exact; if the bounded controls are neutral or leave a cycle, stop and record negative evidence rather than adding register-shaping locals.
safe_actions: authenticate widths and pointer depth before changing order
compare declaration order, initialization point, and first semantic use as separate variables
separate declaration from assignment only when target calls or stores prove the later lifetime boundary
verify that no extsh, clrlwi, spill, frame, call, or relocation debt appears
revert neutral or unresolved register-color probes
examples: endingdll fn_1_12838 became strict exact when sequential same-type loop locals remained in one outer scope and declaration order produced indices in r31/r30/r29 plus group/model in r27/r28
mdbankdll fn_1_13764 changed from 98.833336% to strict exact when natural HU3D_PARTICLE_DATA* data was declared before HU3D_PARTICLE* particle, rotating data/particle from r30/r31 to target r31/r30

mdbankdll fn_1_83CC became strict exact at 756 bytes when the authenticated camera pointer was declared normally but assigned after window/light cleanup, beginning its saved-register lifetime at the target point
mdpresultdll fn_1_B178 became exact when the inner-loop index preceded the outer-loop index in natural declaration chronology
main:board/opening OpeningSingleEffHook became exact after restoring automatic-object and commutative-expression order
main:board/star StarMatHook became exact after restoring the target-proven four-byte and twelve-byte automatic-object order
main:board/config mbPausePanelCreate became exact after declaration-list order resolved its final saved-register swap
main:board/tutorial TutorialWatch and three guide-object call sites became exact after restoring block-scoped value and pointer lifetimes
wave 75 mbev_Scroll and ScrollMain became 100% after declaration-list order removed complete inverse r28/r29 and r30/r31 cycles without changing size, control flow, or relocations

main:board/telop mbTelopTimeSprRotSet proved the GC/2.6 O0 FPR ranking boundary: measured first-sine/second-sine/shared-scale usage 4/4/9 produced the source f29/f30/f31 order, while a diagnostic-only 11/10/9 control produced strict-exact retail f31/f30/f29 at 664 bytes
tools/mwcc_win32_varinfo.py measured mbTelopTimeSprRotSet named VarInfo usage scale/sinFirst/sinSecond = 9/4/4 and allocator assignment scale f31, sinSecond f30, sinFirst f29
counterexamples: meschkdll fn_1_188 improved to an exact-sized 99.893870 form, but legal declaration/scope controls could not break its final dirWin/nextMessNo r20/r22 cycle, so all nonexact probes were reverted.
mdpresultdll fn_1_C358 reproduced the target save set after a separate second-loop index but retained a seven-row register-color cycle, so the function was fully reverted.
main:board/masu mbMasuPlayerColorSet regressed when adjacent partyF and type declarations were swapped, so the probe was reverted.

wave 75 allocation-temporary and narrower-scope declaration probes were byte-neutral, while moving mbMasuPlayerColorSet dayF ahead of type regressed two operand differences to seven; all were reverted.
A guessed initialized write-only Last Five local changed live-register allocation without producing the target stack word, and a ghost saved-GPR local in Wipe lacked source authentication.
Changing a local's width to steer allocation is not this rule; it introduces normalization differences and must be rejected.
Do not split a declaration initializer solely to choose a register when target call/store chronology does not prove a later semantic lifetime.
Do not add redundant temporaries, fake scopes, volatile qualifiers, register keywords, or discarded reads solely to choose registers.

mbTelopTimeSprRotSet reached strict exact only under a discarded-read use-count diagnostic; that proved VarInfo.usage ownership but was rejected and reverted because no authenticated natural source justified those reads.

Splitting mbTelopTimeSprRotSet's shared scale lifetime into natural scale, rotation, and phase locals grew the source from 664 to 696 bytes, added saved f22/f23 lifetimes, and regressed strict matching to 94.27109%; natural chained assignments for the two absolute-value copies were byte-neutral and retained the same twelve f29/f31 operand differences. Both probes were reverted, so do not repeat those allocator axes.

Further mbTelopTimeSprRotSet controls were all negative and reverted: -sym on was text-neutral with the same twelve f29/f31 differences, nested raw-result assignments shrank 664 to 624 bytes, HuAbs grew it to 744 bytes, and standard fabsf grew it to 728 bytes.

A direct-inline fabsf diagnostic was also negative: usage and register roles were unchanged, text grew from 664 to 704 bytes with extra f22/f23 lifetimes, and no MP6 provenance authenticates that helper.

patterns.title: Use chained assignment when one RHS value feeds target-ordered stores
patterns.summary: Repeated MWCC O0 recoveries show that a natural chained assignment can evaluate one authenticated right-hand value or value-producing call once and emit several stores in the target's right-to-left lvalue order, while equivalent independent statements can duplicate a load or immediate and change stack, register, or reload chronology.
patterns.conditions: Use only when target instructions prove one unambiguous RHS evaluation or call, multiple assignments of that result, and a specific value lifetime or store order that independent statements fail to reproduce.

source_condition.change: Express several assignments from one authenticated value-producing expression as one chained assignment rather than independent statements.
requires: identical assignment semantics and compatible destination types
target evidence for one RHS evaluation and every destination store
target-backed right-to-left store chronology
one bounded chained-versus-independent compiler control
exact instructions, relocations, and consumers after the change

possible_changes: one shared immediate, call result, or interpolated value
right-to-left destination stores
removal of a duplicate load or immediate
different stack-object lifetime and reload placement
known_signatures: the target loads one constant once and stores it to adjacent fields in reverse textual destination order
independent statements emit a second li or reload and grow the function
a chained call-result assignment stores two vector components before one target reload
a chained interpolated-value assignment restores both stack layout and component store order
a two-destination call-result chain can preserve the target allocation-result register while a longer chain through a later traversal alias changes the lifetime and regresses

patterns.rule: When the target proves one unambiguous RHS evaluation feeding several assignments, test one natural chained assignment against independent statements. Keep later aliases outside the chain unless the target proves they share that same assignment lifetime. Retain the form only when complete text, relocations, and consumers become exact; never chain unrelated side effects, calls with ambiguous evaluation order, or assignments with different conversion semantics merely to shape registers.
safe_actions: confirm the RHS is evaluated once in the target
compare destination store order and conversion widths
measure one independent-statement control under the pinned owner profile
reject the chain if it changes side-effect order, narrowing, volatile access, or consumer semantics
examples: main:board/star mbStarObjCreate became exact with `work->masuId = work->playerNo = -1`, which emits one li and the target's playerNo-before-masuId stores.

main:board/capsule mbCapInit became 312/312 strict exact with `capsuleBorderObjId = borderObjData = HuMemDirectMallocNum(...)`, while assigning the later traversal alias `borderId = borderObjData` separately preserves the target r25 allocation lifetime.
mdpartydll fn_1_1733C chains one helper result into two vector components before the target reload.
mdpartydll fn_1_B008 directly chains one interpolated scale across three components, restoring target stack layout and store order.
main:board/opening exact closures independently retain target-backed chained zero and player-number assignments.
counterexamples: Two independent mbStarObjCreate statements emitted a second li -1, grew the function, and regressed it to 96.666664%.

Extending the exact mbCapInit chain through `borderId` changed the saved-register and spill shape and regressed to 96.474360%; a successful two-destination chain does not justify adding every later alias.
Do not chain volatile accesses, unrelated function calls, or expressions whose side-effect order is not target-authenticated.
Do not use a chain when destination conversions differ or the target evaluates the RHS more than once.

patterns.title: Test pointer truthiness or literal zero when typed NULL materializes a compare operand
patterns.summary: Across MWCC O0 profiles, a natural pointer truth test or comparison with integer literal 0 can lower to a direct cmplwi, while an equivalent comparison with typed NULL can materialize zero in a register and emit li plus cmplw. An authenticated integer typedef that carries an address can require a consumer-local pointer cast for the reverse transition without changing its public ABI.
patterns.conditions: Use when the target directly compares a proven pointer against immediate zero but the candidate materializes a null operand, when the candidate is exactly four bytes larger for that reason, or when target and independent address-semantics evidence prove that an address-valued integer handle is consumed in the pointer-null domain.

source_condition.change: Select the authenticated integer-zero or pointer-null expression domain for one null guard without changing the producer's public type.
requires: the expression is authenticated as a pointer or as an integer typedef carrying an address
identical null-test semantics
target and candidate compare instructions
exact control flow, relocations, and consumers after the change
independent sibling/header address semantics before casting an integer typedef

possible_changes: direct cmplwi against zero
removal of li r0,0 plus cmplw
introduction of the target li r0,0 plus cmplw for an authenticated address-handle consumer
a four-byte function-size reduction
unchanged branch structure and relocation stream
known_signatures: `if (pointer)` matches cmplwi while `if (pointer != NULL)` emits li plus cmplw
`while (*entry != 0)` is four bytes shorter than `while (*entry != NULL)`
the mismatch is isolated to null materialization and compare operands
integer 0 and 0L remain cmplwi while a consumer-local `(void *)addressHandle == NULL` produces li plus cmplw

patterns.rule: Run one bounded integer-zero versus pointer-null spelling control for an authenticated null guard. Retain the natural form only with exact text, branches, relocations, and consumers. Never cast opaque resource handles or change a public type merely to obtain the compare shape; a consumer-local cast is admissible only for an independently authenticated address-valued integer typedef whose target proves the pointer-domain comparison.
safe_actions: confirm the operand's pointer or address-handle semantics from headers and independent consumers
compare the emitted cmplwi versus li/cmplw sequence
preserve the target branch sense and null semantics
keep an authenticated address-handle typedef and public ABI unchanged when testing a consumer-local cast
revert the spelling change if codegen is neutral or other instructions regress
examples: Ending cleanup callbacks matched target direct cmplwi only with pointer truthiness under GC/2.6
mdbankdll _epilog matched 76 bytes under GC/1.3.2 with `*entry != 0`; typed NULL materialized zero and grew it to 80 bytes
mdpresultdll repeated destructor functions retained natural pointer truthiness plus a terminal local null assignment in a first-build-exact GC/2.6 cluster

mdpartydll fn_1_2B0 and its inline copy in fn_1_400 became exact when the address-valued AMEM_PTR result was cast at the consumer to `(void *)` before comparison with NULL; integer 0 and 0L controls remained cmplwi

Mario Party 4 commit 147b165a83187ac9e6cfdc3bf52f2e73437b1ffd stores a HuAR_DVDtoARAM AMEM_PTR result in a `void *` through an explicit cast in src/game/chrman.c, independently authenticating Hudson address-handle semantics.
counterexamples: An opaque integer resource or non-address handle is not a pointer guard; do not cast it to void* to select cmplw.
An address-sized integer alone is insufficient: require sibling/header consumer proof that the typedef carries an address before testing a cast.
NULL spelling is not globally wrong; use the target compare and authenticated operand type at the specific consumer.
Do not rewrite unrelated condition structure when only the null operand spelling differs.

patterns.title: Stop ordinary, intrinsic block-move, and indexed paired spellings at a displacement-form HuVecF target
patterns.summary: Repeated GC/2.6 board evidence shows that a target HuVecF copy written with displacement-form paired-single loads and stores is not reproduced by aggregate assignment, HuCopyVecF, ordinary memcpy, the documented inline __memcpy compiler intrinsic, a block-local pointer-mediated aggregate assignment, or explicit assignment through the documented __vec2x32float__ type: aggregate and __memcpy forms emit integer word copies, HuCopyVecF emits scalar float copies, ordinary memcpy emits a call, and the paired type emits indexed psq_lx/psq_stx forms. A powerpc-rs ISA-driven census of the current 508-object source corpus found no board or game object containing a non-stack unquantized displacement psq_l or psq_st instruction; all 908 such instructions were confined to 12 Dolphin or MusyX runtime objects. Retained-history archaeology found the matching displacement sequence only inside an MP6_NATIVE_PORT inline-assembly scaffold, not in an organic C helper or historical header. An authenticated boundary audit also excludes SDK PSMTXCopy, which is an explicit-assembly 48-byte matrix routine, and MWCC runtime __copy, which is a called helper for odd-aligned or odd-sized C++ default-copy arrays; neither can explain the inline 12-byte C transfers. Retail-object m2c passes for mbev_Last5, PauseGuideMain, mbObjFadeCreate, and mbObjFadeTexRotSet preserve each scalar z-field store but omit the paired x/y transfer entirely; m2c therefore confirms surrounding field/dataflow but cannot recover or authenticate the original 12-byte source spelling. A cross-title Hudson control narrows the remaining search: Mario Party 4 configures its last5.c as Matching under the same GC/2.6 game flags and identical Vec definition while using the natural aggregate assignment `sp3C = sp48`. This authenticates aggregate assignment as organic source, but does not prove that an isolated assignment must select paired instructions. When the target reuses one source/destination stack-slot pair across several copies while the candidate keeps distinct vectors alive, investigate source-level lifetime and slot reuse before repeating copy-spelling probes. For mbev_Last5 this lifetime consolidation is already exhausted: commit 03741f481d9040666ba02661728a17b666475e27 reuses shared `pos` and `target` locals for all three transfers, improves the strict result, but still emits integer lwz/stw copies instead of the target paired-single displacement sequence. patterns.summary: A source cluster can compile instruction- and relocation-exact in isolation yet be unsafe to bind as a new translation unit: moving its definitions can remove one-pass inline visibility from later callers that were already exact in the original combined source owner. A dependency-closed suffix, predecessor, or interior island can still be bound independently when every outgoing compile-time inline-consumer edge stays in the original translation unit and all protected consumers and pool owners remain exact. Function-address and callback assignments are link-only edges unless a direct compile-time call also exists. Conversely, absence of an incoming target call relocation does not prove that a helper has no consumer: MWCC can auto-inline the call and leave no REL24 edge. patterns.summary: A GC/2.6 -O0 function can retain an initialized scalar whose value is never referenced later, emitting a real prologue stack store while the function's working accumulator remains in a saved register.
