patterns.conditions: Apply whenever exact source covers only a prefix, suffix, or noncontiguous island while adjacent target ranges remain on autogenerated retail fallback; compare both sides of every candidate symbol boundary before widening a source span.

source_condition.change: Recover, consolidate, or promote C that replaces part of a DTK fallback span.
requires: target section boundaries and relocations for the generated owner
per-function strict/data/relocation rows for the exact island and each adjacent target span
explicit separation between build partition and semantic/original owner
a pinned map, debug record, source blob, or equivalent provenance before claiming an original filename
full object and retail verification after any path or ownership change

possible_changes: build-object subdivision around a source-linked island
an increased build-object denominator without new original owners
a reduced matching-object count after synthetic islands are collapsed without losing recovered source or exact-function evidence
one canonical MWCC text csect concatenating recovered functions that the target separates with fallback gaps
an exact island can coexist with an adjacent fallback function without promoting the surrounding object
repository path churn with no target-binary evidence
known_signatures: a filename contains a recovery iteration number absent from every target and source-provenance artifact
one original application range is represented by several generated C objects separated by fallback spans
moving discontiguous exact islands into one canonical file makes their emitted text contiguous and displaces intervening target fallback ranges
W11 under GC/1.3.2: fn_1_1454 is 304/304 strict+data exact with one mbHermiteCalc REL24 while adjacent fn_1_12FC is +16 bytes/+3 relocations
renaming the source path leaves compiled and linked retail bytes unchanged

patterns.rule: Use recovery pass numbers and address islands only in ignored evidence and queue metadata. Do not add or promote pass, tail, extra, or address-derived C shard paths. Consolidate recovered C into an authenticated canonical owner. If the translation unit is incomplete, configure the whole application owner as NonMatching, retain relocation-aware exact-subset evidence without calling it source-linked, and require a byte-identical retail build; mark the owner Matching only after its complete compiler, data, relocation, and consumer closure is exact. When a split deliberately isolates a symbol-boundary island, keep every adjacent nonexact symbol on target fallback and never promote the surrounding object from the island's score.
safe_actions: keep partial-island probes under ignored build evidence rather than tracked source
record the semantic owner and temporary build partition as separate evidence fields
retain address-derived function symbols until naming evidence exists
compare exact island and adjacent target spans independently before changing a split boundary
restore or extend the authenticated canonical owner only after declaration chronology, inline closure, data ownership, and retail output remain exact
treat consolidation of historical shards as a verified ownership change, not a cosmetic bulk rename
keep exact-function counts independent from configured build-object counts when an incomplete canonical owner uses whole-owner fallback
record the linked REL hash alongside the island's strict/data and relocation proof
run the complete-file promotion gate before READY
examples: Existing pass, tail, and application_<address> files record earlier build partitioning only. They are migration debt, not original filename evidence and not templates for new recovery.

A repository-wide consolidation removed 174 synthetic C files across endingdll, mdbankdll, mdpresultdll, mdsingdll, miraclebookdll, openingDll, optionDll, s02Dll, and staffdll. Their authenticated canonical owners retained 538 of 648 exact source functions while all 137 retail outputs remained byte-identical.

An incomplete canonical application owner stays NonMatching as one unit. Exact functions in its compiled comparison object remain recovery evidence, but they do not inflate the configured matching-object count.
W11 under GC/1.3.2 retained fn_1_1454 as a symbol-boundary 304/304 strict+data exact island with one REL24 to mbHermiteCalc; the linked w11 REL remained SHA1 7718483b2764d53433edbe72ca4abc3c686629bc.
counterexamples: A filename preserved in a pinned original map, debug record, or authenticated same-game source blob is provenance and may be used with its confidence stated.
An address-bound shard name is deliberately neutral, but it still is not an original filename claim.
Do not merge noncontiguous shards merely to make the tree look original when the compiler closure or unresolved fallback gaps would regress.
W11 fn_1_12FC remained target fallback at +16 bytes/+3 relocations; its mismatch is not permission to widen the exact fn_1_1454 island.

patterns.title: Recover the smallest authenticated semantic aggregate prefix before using an opaque overlay
patterns.summary: When an exact function reaches only early fields of a large private engine object, the target displacement and an authenticated same-game layout can justify a natural nested prefix through the last accessed field. This preserves semantic field access without importing a broad historically unproven header or inventing byte padding for the unseen suffix.
patterns.conditions: Use when target instructions authenticate one or more early nested fields, a canonical same-game layout agrees on the prefix order and types, and the complete private structure or historical include closure is not yet proven.

source_condition.change: Replace an offset-only cast or incomplete opaque object view with the smallest natural aggregate prefix that reaches every target-accessed field.
requires: target load/store widths and displacements for every accessed field
authenticated same-game type order and field types through the final accessed field
no invented padding, anonymous byte arrays, or claims about the unseen suffix
exact text, relocations, protected consumers, and linked retail output

possible_changes: natural nested field-address materialization
correct signedness and load/store width
no visibility from unrelated declarations in a broad public header
known_signatures: an offset-only access matches the address but obscures a stable nested position, rotation, or scale field
a broad header changes code generation or section ownership beyond the accessed fields
a minimal prefix reproduces the target displacement and keeps neighboring exact functions unchanged

patterns.rule: Prefer the smallest authenticated semantic prefix through the last accessed field over an opaque offset overlay. Keep the remaining suffix incomplete and private, and promote a shared header only after all consumers, declaration chronology, data ownership, and retail output prove the wider closure.
safe_actions: derive each prefix boundary from target displacements and access widths
reuse canonical same-game public subtypes such as vectors and transforms
keep the prefix owner-local until independent consumers prove shared header closure
compare preprocessing and every protected consumer before broadening visibility
revert the type hypothesis if any field offset, relocation, or exact neighbor regresses
examples: Opening guide and character helpers reached HSF object mesh.base scale, rotation, and position fields through an owner-local HSF object/mesh/transform prefix. Ten functions, 2,612 text bytes, and 167 physical relocations became exact without opaque padding or a broad HSF header.
counterexamples: One matching displacement does not authenticate the field name or the complete enclosing type.
Do not extend the prefix beyond the final target-accessed field merely to resemble a modern header.
Do not replace unknown suffix bytes with padding fields and call the resulting layout recovered.

patterns.title: Inventory uncovered target intervals instead of trusting recovery ledgers
patterns.summary: A function can already have exact recovered C while still being absent from the active split configuration. Historical function counts, recovery reports, and source-file presence therefore do not prove that a target interval is currently source-linked. The authoritative inventory is the target function extent set minus the union of registered source split intervals.
patterns.conditions: Apply before ranking remaining functions in any partially source-linked DOL or REL owner, especially after several recovery batches or when generated fallback spans have been repeatedly subdivided.

source_condition.change: Build the remaining-work inventory or select a new exact source island.
requires: target function starts and sizes from the pinned symbol/split catalog
the current registered source intervals from splits.txt
normalization of overlapping or adjacent configured intervals
confirmation that every candidate extent is not already covered by a source-linked object

possible_changes: discovery of an exact but unregistered source sliver
removal of already configured functions from the recovery queue
a corrected denominator when fallback spans are subdivided around the missing interval
known_signatures: a source definition and old exact report exist but no current splits.txt interval covers the function
two registered source intervals leave a target-function-sized gap between them
a recovery ledger count disagrees with configured object coverage

patterns.rule: Compute remaining work from target extents minus current source-linked split intervals. Treat source files and historical exact ledgers as evidence to inspect, not as configuration truth. Register a recovered gap only after its current object, relocations, consumers, and retail output are reverified.
safe_actions: parse the pinned target symbols and current splits before scoring candidates
subtract complete half-open source intervals rather than matching filenames or pass numbers
flag exact-source/unregistered-target discrepancies as high-leverage integration candidates
re-run object and consumer proof because an old exact report can be stale
report fixed recovered bytes separately from the changing build-object denominator
examples: optionDll fn_1_18B8 had exact recovered C in historical combined source but remained unregistered in the 0x18B8..0x18D8 gap between two configured owners. Interval subtraction found and source-linked the 32-byte callback with one exact relocation.
counterexamples: A source file under src/ does not prove that its target range is linked by the active build.
A prior exact-function total is not an interval map and can silently omit or double-count ownership after later splits.
Do not infer original translation-unit boundaries from the generated intervals.

patterns.title: Separate split assignment, source-body presence, and exact emission
patterns.summary: After recovery shards are consolidated, one canonical NonMatching source owner can be assigned the module's complete target interval even though the C file defines only a subset of target functions and only a smaller subset has fresh instruction and relocation proof. An empty target-minus-split interval set therefore proves configuration geometry, not recovery completion.
patterns.conditions: Apply whenever splits.txt assigns a complete application text range to one NonMatching source owner, especially after pass, tail, extra, or address-derived recovery shards were collapsed into the canonical file.

source_condition.change: Inventory remaining recovery or declare a consolidated canonical owner complete.
requires: target function starts and sizes from the pinned symbol catalog
current configured ownership intervals from splits.txt
a source parser that distinguishes target function definitions from declarations, imports, and compiler-generated entry points
fresh per-function instruction and relocation comparison for every source-defined candidate
consumer and linked-retail replay before upgrading the owner from NonMatching

possible_changes: a zero-byte geometric split gap while many target functions remain body-missing
a source-present function remaining unproven or non-exact in the canonical translation unit
a historical exact shard regressing after consolidation because declaration chronology, inline visibility, or literal-pool ownership changed
different denominators for configured ownership, source-body coverage, and freshly exact recovery
known_signatures: splits.txt assigns the full application range to one NonMatching C file
symbols.txt contains more target function rows than the canonical source defines
the owner exact-function aggregate is smaller than the source-definition count
target-minus-split subtraction is empty while declarations or imports still stand in for target bodies

patterns.rule: Maintain three independent ledgers: configured split assignment, target functions with canonical C bodies, and target functions freshly proven instruction-, relocation-, consumer-, and retail-exact. Use target-minus-split subtraction only for configuration gaps. For recovery debt inside a whole-range NonMatching owner, compare target symbols with actual source definitions, then subtract only freshly exact emitted functions. Never convert historical shard status or full-range split ownership into an exact-function claim.
safe_actions: report configured interval coverage, source-body coverage, and fresh exact coverage as separate counts and byte totals
rank body-missing target functions before source-present mismatch work when both are otherwise dependency-closed
preserve compiler-generated prolog and epilog accounting separately from authored C bodies
replay historical exact subsets in the canonical translation unit before retaining their counts
keep unresolved target functions on fallback without creating recovery shard files
examples: miraclebookdll assigns the complete application text range 0x0..0x99D8 to miraclebook.c, so geometric interval subtraction is empty, yet the 39 target rows include six directly body-missing fn_1_* definitions and the current owner aggregate still reports eight absent-or-not-exact functions totaling 20,484 text bytes.
mdbankdll assigns 0x0..0x137DC to mdbank.c while 36 target fn_1_* rows totaling 43,916 text bytes have no canonical C body. Full split ownership does not recover those bodies.

mdsingdll assigns 0x0..0x35300 to mdsing.c while the canonical source defines 92 of 285 target fn_1_* rows; the other 193 rows remain body-missing even though no configured text interval is uncovered.
counterexamples: A genuinely unregistered exact island such as optionDll fn_1_18B8 is still found by target-minus-split subtraction; this rule does not replace the configuration-gap inventory.
A complete split interval is not an exactness report, and a function declaration is not a recovered body.
A historical Matching shard does not remain exact automatically after its body moves into a larger canonical translation unit.

patterns.title: Preserve empty REL aliases without inventing source owners
patterns.summary: Some MP6 overlay names are deliberately empty REL aliases. Their catalog exposes only ctor and dtor section labels, generated configuration has no module units, and the build links the shared zero-byte REL/empty.c object. The overlay name and loader entry do not authenticate a dedicated C translation unit.
patterns.conditions: Apply when an REL catalog has no text functions, no data objects, no source history, and generated module configuration links only the shared empty object. The current proof covers storyresultdll and partyresultdll.

source_condition.change: Classify an apparently source-less REL or propose creating a new canonical owner for it.
requires: symbols and splits proving the absence of text, rodata, data, and bss target extents
configured unit inventory proving that only the shared empty object is linked
repository history confirming that no dedicated source owner existed
loader and resource references classified as module-name consumers rather than source-owner evidence
fresh linked retail proof before changing an existing empty-module classification

possible_changes: a named REL with zero recoverable application text and no runtime owner
two overlay aliases sharing the same expected target hash
a loader-table entry without any callable function or owned data
an invented nonempty object changing section layout and retail bytes
known_signatures: symbols.txt contains only _ctors and _dtors labels
splits.txt declares ctor and dtor sections but assigns no source ranges
generated module units are empty and the link consumes REL/empty.o
no src/REL/<module> path exists in current history

patterns.rule: Treat a proven empty REL alias as a closed zero-sized module, not as an unrecovered canonical C owner. Keep the shared zero-byte REL/empty.c infrastructure and stable module catalog entry. Do not create module-specific C, runtime, generated shard, data, or semantic function names unless new target extents and authenticated source ownership are discovered.
safe_actions: exclude proven empty aliases from remaining function and byte denominators
record loader and data-directory references as module consumers without inferring code ownership
compare alias symbols, splits, configured units, and expected hashes before classifying an empty module
report unknown physical relocation totals as unknown rather than inventing zero from a sparse catalog
require fresh retail replay before modifying shared empty-object linkage
examples: storyresultdll has no text function or data-object rows, no dedicated source path, and its generated module has no units while linking the shared empty object.
partyresultdll has the same empty symbols and splits and the same expected target hash as storyresultdll, corroborating an intentional empty overlay alias rather than missing recovered code.
counterexamples: resultDll is not an empty alias: its target catalog contains application text and data extents even though no source owner is currently authenticated.
A loader-table DLL name does not by itself prove that a dedicated C file existed.
Do not report a fresh byte-identical retail result from expected hashes or generated build rules alone.

patterns.title: Use the recovered capsule-effect random-float macro with authored shift spelling
patterns.summary: MP6 board capsule effects normalize `mbRandMod(1 << 28)` by 2^-28 through the shared `MBCapsuleEffRandF()` source macro. The bound and scaling are target-authenticated, but repeating either a raw power-of-two immediate or the exponent-form reciprocal at call sites is compiler/decompiler-shaped rather than credible authored source. The macro name and source role continue the direct MP5 capsule-header interface, while MP6 changes the underlying generator from the MP5 mask-based expression to `mbRandMod`.
patterns.conditions: Apply only to MP6 board capsule-effect consumers whose target calls `mbRandMod` with 268435456 and multiplies the converted result by 2^-28. The current proof covers Capevent, Capspecial, and the five strict-exact Capmove Kinoko variants under GC/2.6; prove additional consumers independently before widening the header fan-out.

source_condition.change: Replace a complete `mbRandMod(1 << 28)` times 2^-28 expansion with `MBCapsuleEffRandF()` from `game/board/capsule.h`.
requires: the target call argument 268435456
the target float constant 2^-28 and matching integer-to-float conversion
unchanged call count and evaluation order
byte-identical source-object instruction, section, and relocation reports before and after the macro recovery
a consumer-specific check before adding the shared header to another translation unit

possible_changes: no object change when the macro replaces the complete authenticated expansion
different random distribution if incorrectly replaced with `frandf()`
different floating operand or pool chronology if only part of the expansion is rewritten
known_signatures: materialize 268435456 as the `mbRandMod` argument
call relocation to `mbRandMod`
integer-to-float conversion followed by an `lfs` of 2^-28 and `fmuls`
Capevent and Capspecial relocation-aware objdiff JSON remains byte-for-byte identical across 122 converted call sites

patterns.rule: Use `MBCapsuleEffRandF()` for the authenticated MP6 capsule-effect normalization instead of retaining the expanded reciprocal. Spell its power-of-two bound as `1 << 28`, not as a raw hexadecimal literal, and retain `1.0f / (1 << 28)` instead of an exponent-form constant. Do not substitute `frandf()`, do not infer this macro from an arbitrary 0..1 random expression, and do not claim the macro in another owner until its full object and relocation stream is unchanged.
safe_actions: match the complete call-plus-normalization signature before replacing it
include the narrow recovered `game/board/capsule.h` interface
compare complete relocation-aware reports before and after the source-form cleanup
preserve expression evaluation order around every macro call
extend the card's owner scope only after another consumer reproduces the byte-neutral result
examples: Capevent converted 118 complete expansions to `MBCapsuleEffRandF()` while its full relocation-aware report stayed SHA-256 6052b0c2ad53f418164f3fe9af2de0fb98c2db47a6734bc93ae962cbf8700d8b before and after; all 160 strict-exact functions and 33,500 exact bytes were preserved.

Capspecial converted four complete expansions while its full relocation-aware report stayed SHA-256 eab8958fe84da8db3ee13f03793d196b73829b1643f7f6fd8d6696b0d41e0290 before and after; all 18 strict-exact functions were preserved.

Capmove's five Kinoko variants are strict-exact across 6,756 text bytes with the shared macro at every target-authenticated random normalization call; the complete owner retained 17/24 strict-exact functions with zero regressions.

Replacing the header body's raw bound with `1 << 28` and the reciprocal with `1.0f / (1 << 28)` preserved the complete Capevent object SHA-256 c1c4977e76666cbb07e68ae7a8f1ce74bf9c190bb03898dfd0b0bd8bd17d9535 and Capspecial object SHA-256 7af0047e5581ef3f4596b9556c8d37f346c7911727df53f430a65e78fb01f554.

Mario Party 5 commit e246f9d9850ff53ac684b971068fbf87fdcf6acb defines the direct predecessor `MBCapsuleEffRandF()` interface in `include/game/board/capsule.h`; MP6 retains the MBCapsule family but authenticates a different mbRandMod-based expansion.
counterexamples: `frandf()` also returns a float near [0,1), but it uses a different bit mapping and is not interchangeable with the target's `mbRandMod(1 << 28)` call.
A long exponent literal can describe the emitted float value, but target bytes cannot prove that literal was present in authored source.
Do not use the MP5 mask-and-127 macro body in MP6; only the interface name and capsule-effect role carry across titles, while the MP6 target proves the new body.

patterns.title: Keep one OR continuation in the loop condition when the target has one shared backedge
patterns.summary: Under GC/2.6 O0, a natural `for` loop whose continuation is the logical OR of a frame bound and a completion predicate emits one shared condition block and one body backedge. Splitting the same semantics into nested or consecutive loops changes the unconditional branch destination even when the calls and computations agree.
patterns.conditions: Use only when target CFG evidence shows one initialization edge into a shared two-predicate condition, either true predicate enters the same body, and the body has one increment/backedge. The repeatable proof is the five strict-exact Capmove Kinoko variants.

source_condition.change: Express the target-backed frame-bound and completion predicates together as one `for` continuation using logical OR.
requires: identical loop semantics and side-effect order
target CFG with one shared condition block and one body backedge
one bounded comparison against the nested or split-loop source shape
exact instructions, branches, relocations, and owner neighbors

possible_changes: one shared condition block for both continuation predicates
one unconditional body backedge
different branch destination under nested or split loops
unchanged calls and arithmetic around the loop body
known_signatures: an exact-sized candidate differs only in an unconditional branch destination
the target checks the frame bound and completion state before one shared body
five sibling variants close with the same single-for OR-condition spelling

patterns.rule: When the target CFG proves one shared OR continuation and one backedge, test the natural single-`for` spelling once. Retain it only with exact instructions, relocations, and semantics; do not introduce dead branches, duplicated predicates, or loop restructuring merely to redirect a branch.
safe_actions: draw the target condition and backedge before changing C
compare one single-for form against one nested or split-loop control
verify predicate evaluation and side effects are unchanged
stop after a neutral or negative control instead of forcing the branch
examples: mbev_CapKinoko, mbev_CapSKinoko, mbev_CapPKinoko, mbev_CapMKinoko, and mbev_CapNKinoko are strict-exact across 6,756 text bytes with `i < 60.0f || !check` retained in one for-condition.
counterexamples: A branch-destination residual alone does not authorize changing loop semantics; the complete target CFG must show the shared OR condition.
Do not add a dead branch, duplicate a predicate, or split a side-effecting condition to force one branch target.
A nested or split-loop form that is byte-neutral or better for another owner is owner-local counterevidence, not a reason to generalize this card.

patterns.title: Name numeric identifier domains before emitting recovered C
patterns.summary: Raw numeric hexadecimal literals are forbidden in recovered C. Message IDs, sound IDs, unlock IDs, flags, attributes, and similar target values must be expressed through behavior- or catalog-authenticated named constants. Converting an unexplained hexadecimal value to anonymous decimal only hides the same semantic debt, and complete-file promotion prevents older literals in a touched owner from bypassing the rule.
patterns.conditions: Apply whenever recovered C would pass a numeric identifier, bit mask, resource index, message number, sound number, unlock number, or protocol value that was previously written as a hexadecimal literal.

source_condition.change: Replace a raw numeric target value with an existing named interface constant or a narrowly scoped named enum/macro whose domain and role are authenticated.
requires: target instruction and relocation proof for the emitted numeric value
consumer, resource-catalog, message-catalog, flag, or same-game interface evidence for the constant's domain
a name no more specific than the proven behavior
exact object, relocation, protected-consumer, and retail output after the source-form change

possible_changes: no emitted change when the named integral constant has the same type and value
changed promotion or compare behavior if an enum's type or signedness is wrong
a false appearance of semantic recovery if only the number base changes
known_signatures: a raw 0x-prefixed token appears in a changed recovered C line
the target value belongs to a repeated API argument domain such as message, sound, unlock, flag, or attribute
an exact named enum initializer emits the same immediate and relocation stream

patterns.rule: Do not promote a recovered C file containing raw hexadecimal literals. Prefer an authenticated existing header symbol; otherwise use the narrowest behavior- or catalog-backed local named constant with a non-hex initializer. Do not convert to anonymous decimal, do not invent a semantic name beyond the evidence, and leave the owner blocked when every touched-file literal domain cannot be established.
safe_actions: search catalogs, sibling consumers, and existing headers for the exact value and API domain
name local enum constants from the proven role when no shared interface is authenticated
keep the constant owner-local until header fanout and include chronology are proven
run the complete-file source-quality gate and an explicit raw-hex scan before READY
recompare every exact object and linked retail consumer after replacing the literal
examples: MDBank message identifiers now use catalog-backed MESSNUM expressions, while unlock and transition-sound identifiers use narrow behavior-backed enums. Across MDBank and MiracleBook, 12 scoped raw literals were removed while 4 changed functions, 12,832 text bytes, 1,412 physical relocations, and all 33 protected consumers remained exact.
MiracleBook transition sound names are bounded by the exact transition states that consume them; they remain behavioral constants, not original symbol claims.
counterexamples: Address-derived symbols and evidence reports may use hexadecimal addresses because they are identity/provenance records, not authored recovered C values.
An existing SDK or authenticated game header constant is preferred and does not become raw merely because its definition is ultimately numeric.
Do not give an unknown number a confident semantic name solely to pass the gate.

patterns.title: Probe complete truthful void-prototype visibility as one register-allocation set
patterns.summary: Under GC/2.6 at O0,p, a translation unit can retain the right control flow and call identities yet miss register allocation across a large function when target-called void functions are implicit or otherwise lack their authenticated visible prototypes. Shop proves that restoring the complete declaration set can close the function even when partial subsets are neutral or regress.
patterns.conditions: Use when a large GC/2.6 function has mostly aligned control flow and relocations, the residuals cluster around call-result handling or live ranges, and one or more called void functions lack visible authoritative declarations. Treat the declarations as a coordinated translation-unit variable rather than assuming each prototype has an independent local effect.

source_condition.change: Restore the complete authenticated visible prototypes or narrow headers for target-called void functions, preserving the retail translation unit's macro and inline-body visibility.
requires: authoritative same-game signatures for every restored function
a call inventory proving which declarations are absent, implicit, or conflicting
a bounded partial-versus-complete declaration-set matrix
full function instruction and relocation comparison
protected exact-function checks for the complete owner

possible_changes: suppression of implicit integer return handling
call-adjacent temporary lifetimes
GPR and FPR allocation across later basic blocks
function size without changing call identities
whole-function closure only after the final declaration joins the set
known_signatures: control-flow and relocation topology are already close while register assignments remain widespread
individual truthful prototypes produce small, neutral, or negative changes
the complete truthful set removes all instruction differences
broad headers risk unrelated macro, inline-body, or local-data visibility changes

patterns.rule: Inventory and restore all authenticated void-call prototypes as a set before reshaping source around residual register differences. Prefer the narrowest historically plausible headers plus truthful local declarations, test partial and complete sets, and retain only the complete source form that preserves every protected function. Never misdeclare a return type, preserve an implicit declaration, or add fake uses to force allocation.
safe_actions: enumerate calls whose visible declaration is absent or conflicts with symbol authority
recover signatures from authoritative same-game headers and sibling consumers
toggle declaration groups in a bounded matrix under the pinned compiler command
compare target/source bytes, instruction rows, and non-R_PPC_NONE relocations
re-run the full owner report because header visibility can affect neighboring exact functions
examples: For ev_Shop, preliminary truthful layer/camera declarations reached 96.589516%. A 256-combination matrix over eight declaration toggles covering nine additional real void functions closed only with the complete set: 5,876/5,876 bytes, 1,469/1,469 instructions, and 384/384 non-R_PPC_NONE text relocations.
The near-complete add-127 subset remained 98.546630%, demonstrating that a strong partial result did not identify the final declaration independently.
The completed shopevent owner report retained all prior exact functions and advanced from 11/13 to 12/13 strict-exact functions; only ev_ShopSelect remains unpaired.
counterexamples: Do not infer that a broad modern header was visible in retail merely because all of its declarations are correct; gc132-broad-header-visibility records owner-local regressions from excess visibility.
Do not keep an implicit declaration because it happens to improve a score; the positive result requires the truthful complete prototype set.
One exact owner establishes this as a contextual probe, not a compiler-wide guarantee that adding void prototypes always improves output.

patterns.title: Treat pool-data mode as a translation-unit ownership profile
patterns.summary: Selmenu, boot opening, Filesel save, and mdparty stage prove across GC/2.6 and GC/1.3.2 that pool-data mode controls far more than visible literal pooling. Removing pool_data off can broadly regress text, relocations, and BSS while leaving literal data unchanged; the equivalent final compiler option restores the complete target object without retaining a source pragma.
patterns.conditions: Apply when an owner uses pool_data off, removing a pooling control changes apparently unrelated functions or uninitialized data, or a natural source cleanup needs to move a compiler-mode declaration out of C.

source_condition.change: Remove a source pool_data pragma or change the final pooldata option for one translation unit.
requires: the exact final compiler command for the owner
whole-object text, data, rodata, BSS, and relocation comparison
protected constant-free functions as controls
linked retail output after moving the mode into the owner profile

possible_changes: automatic constant propagation across function boundaries
large text-size and relocation-count changes
BSS size and symbol-order changes
regressions in functions that contain no visible pooled literal
known_signatures: pool_data removal changes many direct loads into folded immediates
relocation volume drops globally rather than only near literal users
BSS symbols reorder or change extent under the alternate mode
the configured -pooldata off option restores every affected section and relocation

patterns.rule: Treat pool-data mode as part of the translation unit's authenticated compiler profile, not as a local literal-formatting preference. When target evidence requires pooldata off, record it in the owner's final compile command rather than recovered C, then reverify the complete object and linked retail container.
safe_actions: compare the exact configured command with and without the final pooldata option
include constant-free protected functions in the control set
compare BSS symbol order and physical relocation counts, not only text
move the mode to the narrowest Object extra_cflags entry
reject a project-wide flag change when only one owner is authenticated
examples: For selmenu.c, removing pool_data off changed text from 20,524 to 17,312 bytes, physical relocations from 1,851 to 971, and BSS from 176 to 174 bytes while regressing 14 functions. Adding -pooldata off to that Object restored 25/25 exact functions, every section, all 1,851 relocations, and the retail-identical REL.

For bootDll opening.c, removing the source pragma without an owner flag left rodata, data, and BSS exact but reduced text to 82.831894% with only 19/37 functions exact. Moving -pooldata off to the opening Object restored 37/37 functions, all four owned sections, 1,928 physical relocations, and retail-identical bootDll.rel and main.dol outputs while raising source organicity from 83 to 97.

For fileseldll saveload.c, moving pool_data off into the Object profile preserved all 23 functions, 11,856 text bytes, 831 relocations, and every owned section while contributing to a source-organicity increase from 40 to 96; all 137 retail outputs remained exact.

For GC/1.3.2 mdpartydll stage.c, removing pool_data off without an owner flag left only 34/57 functions exact and reduced text similarity to 82.38697% while rodata, data, and BSS stayed exact. Moving -pooldata off into the Object profile restored all 57 functions, 29,656 text bytes, every owned data section, and the retail-identical REL without a source pragma.
counterexamples: This owner-specific proof does not justify enabling pooldata off for every GC/2.6 object.
A function with no obvious literals is not a valid control by itself because the mode can change cross-function data ownership and propagation.
Do not retain a source pragma merely because text bytes match when an authenticated owner-local compiler profile reproduces the complete object.

patterns.title: Compare the retail function inventory before treating a seam as the only residual
patterns.summary: A stub or seam ledger can name the exported entry point while omitting static helper bodies that belong to the same retail object. Small object size and a short seam list therefore do not bound the remaining reconstruction work. The authoritative first pass is a function-by-function comparison of retail symbol extents against actual source definitions and configured ownership.
patterns.conditions: Apply whenever a supposedly final seam remains far from exact, an owner is described as small or nearly complete, or the source definition count has not been reconciled with the retail object's complete function inventory.

source_condition.change: Rank or begin recovery for a residual seam or partial owner.
requires: the complete retail function-start and size inventory for the object
the translation unit's actual function definitions rather than declarations
the active source-link or split ownership configuration
the byte extent and call relationships of every missing helper

possible_changes: discovery of unimplemented static helper families hidden behind one visible seam
a corrected remaining-function and remaining-byte denominator
bulk recovery of dependency helpers before final entry-point reconciliation
identification of declaration-only placeholders that were mistaken for implementations
known_signatures: the retail object contains more function symbols than the source contains definitions
the visible seam calls static functions that are only forward-declared
the source text deficit is much larger than the visible seam's size delta
a small owner remains unexpectedly difficult after repeated single-function probes

patterns.rule: Before probing the visible seam, subtract the source definition inventory from the complete retail function inventory and reconcile the result with active ownership. Treat every missing static helper as real recovery work, cluster helpers by call relationship, and report both missing function count and missing retail bytes. Do not infer completeness from object size, forward declarations, source-file presence, or a seam ledger alone.
safe_actions: list every retail function symbol with its exact extent
count actual source function bodies separately from prototypes
sum the retail bytes of missing definitions before selecting workers
assign distinct missing helper families to separate workers
rebuild and diff the complete owner after integrating the helper cluster
examples: The Last5 seam looked like one residual in a small board object, but retail last5.o contained 10 functions and 9,304 text bytes while the source contained only six function bodies. Four absent static helpers represented 3,852 retail bytes: Last5RouletteCreate, Last5RouletteOMExec, ev_Last5CapsuleAdd5, and ev_Last5Koopa. Recovering that family in one pass raised the reconstructed source to all 10 function bodies before final byte reconciliation.
counterexamples: A forward declaration is not a recovered function body.
A seam ledger is a priority list, not a complete object symbol inventory.
A small object can still require several kilobytes of missing helper reconstruction.
Do not count generated retail fallback coverage as a source definition.

patterns.title: Move proven owner-wide no-auto-inline policy out of recovered C
patterns.summary: A GC/2.6 owner whose target contains no automatic helper expansion can express that compilation policy once as the final Object option instead of surrounding recovered functions with source dont_inline pragmas. Filesel saveload proves that -inline noauto removes the pragma region at zero instruction, section, or relocation cost.
patterns.conditions: Apply only when removing source dont_inline controls changes automatic expansion and a final owner-local -inline noauto option restores the complete object without suppressing any target-authenticated inline closure.

source_condition.change: Remove one or more source dont_inline pragma regions and set the final auto-inline mode for exactly one translation unit.
requires: the exact final compiler command
whole-object function, section, and relocation comparison
an inventory of helper-call relocations and expanded helper bodies
a linked retail build covering every configured output

possible_changes: small helpers remain calls instead of automatic expansions
caller frame and register allocation remain stable when the target has no auto-inline closure
broad regressions when any target caller requires an automatic expansion
known_signatures: removing a local dont_inline region alone expands one or more helpers
the final -inline noauto option restores every target call relocation and owned section
explicit SDK inline bodies remain governed separately from automatic function selection

patterns.rule: Prefer the narrowest verified Object compiler profile over recovered-C dont_inline pragmas when the policy is owner-wide. Reject the profile immediately if any target-authenticated automatic expansion, function byte, section byte, or relocation regresses.
safe_actions: compare the owner with pragmas, without pragmas, and with the final noauto profile
inspect every changed call edge rather than checking only the pragma-adjacent function
record the final option after the ordinary owner flags so its precedence is explicit
keep the source control when the target requires mixed automatic-inline behavior and no natural chronology is proven
examples: fileseldll saveload.c removed its dont_inline region and compiled with final -inline noauto while retaining 23/23 exact functions, 11,856 text bytes, 831 relocations, exact rodata/data, and the retail-identical fileseldll.rel.
counterexamples: Mode-select chronology includes a target-authenticated nested automatic expansion; blanket dont_inline suppresses it, so an owner-wide noauto profile is invalid there.

GC/1.3.2 mdpartydll requires mixed automatic-inline behavior: removing the scoped fn_1_BB30 boundary expands it into fn_1_BBD8, while an owner-wide -inline noauto profile leaves only 84 of 258 functions exact. Keep the narrow source boundary when no natural chronology reproduces that mixed target.
Do not infer an owner-wide policy from one exact leaf function or from unchanged text size alone.

patterns.title: Preserve repeated target call or access skeletons before abstraction
patterns.summary: A nearby helper or wrapper can be semantically equivalent yet compile differently from a retail sibling family that repeats a direct memory lookup or a long ordered call skeleton. The repeated target skeleton is stronger reconstruction evidence than a source-level desire to share the work.
patterns.conditions: Apply when several sibling functions differ together, the target repeats one direct access skeleton or at least six meaningful calls in the same order, and the recovered source routes those functions through another accessor, helper, or short wrapper.

source_condition.change: Replace an unauthenticated helper or wrapper route with the repeated target-backed direct access or call skeleton using recovered structures and existing named domain constants.
requires: the same target access skeleton or a long ordered meaningful-call overlap across the sibling family
authenticated structure fields, index calculation, and called API roles
a multi-function object comparison
a negative control from any neighboring family with a different copy or return shape

possible_changes: restored instruction scheduling and register lifetimes across several siblings
removal of an extra accessor call, wrapper call, or inlined abstraction shape
regression when an aggregate-return sibling genuinely uses a different compiler pattern
known_signatures: several scalar setters share the same residual and become exact from one direct lookup form
the target repeats bank selection, slot selection, and object pointer loading in every sibling
neighboring vector getters regress under the same rewrite because their aggregate-copy skeleton differs
a short wrapper expands into the same clamp, per-item update, sound, and sleep chronology already present in two longer siblings

patterns.rule: When a sibling family has a repeated target-backed call or access skeleton, preserve that skeleton in each function instead of routing through a merely equivalent helper or wrapper. Apply the rewrite only to the homogeneous family and stop at the first neighboring function whose target calls, copy behavior, or return shape differs.
safe_actions: cluster siblings by ordered target calls and memory-access skeleton before editing
use recovered field names and existing named domain constants in the repeated lookup
compile and compare the whole sibling cluster after one source-form change
probe one structurally different neighbor as a bounded negative control
retain only strict-exact gains with zero regressions
examples: Restoring the repeated direct coin bank and slot lookup closed eight scalar Coin object accessors at once: 1,040 strict-exact text bytes with no exact-function regression.

Replacing mbCoinAddExec's short wrapper with the target-proven clamp, per-coin update, sound, and sleep skeleton recovered 288 of its 304 target bytes; the remaining 16 bytes are saved-register and local-stack lifetime differences.
counterexamples: The adjacent position, rotation, and scale getters use aggregate-copy behavior; forcing the scalar direct-lookup rewrite onto them regressed the object and was reverted.
Do not duplicate a lookup merely because several functions share a file or structure type; the target skeleton itself must be repeated.
A long list of calls is not enough when the meaningful ordered overlap is short, generic, or belongs to different behavioral families.

patterns.title: Revalidate and remove stale library-guard exceptions after include changes
patterns.summary: A previously measured library-header guard override can become codegen-neutral after the translation unit's include graph changes. Last5, Mgcall, Capevent, and Coin retained byte-identical candidate objects after `_MATH_H` was deleted, so keeping the override and its exception would preserve compiler-control debt without preserving any target output.
patterns.conditions: Apply only to a recovered translation unit that already contains a library-header guard override with recorded historical evidence, after its include set or header coexistence rules have changed. This is a removal probe, never authority to introduce a guard.

source_condition.change: Delete the recovered-C library guard override while leaving the natural SDK header include in place.
requires: a candidate-object hash captured immediately before the probe
one serialized rebuild under the pinned owner compiler command
the complete candidate-object hash after the rebuild
strict and data-value owner reports with protected exact-function checks
full-file organicity and source-quality checks

possible_changes: no object change when current headers already provide the required coexistence boundary
reappearance of weak math constants or declaration-ABI changes when the override is still active
removal of a compiler-control organicity finding when the override is obsolete
known_signatures: the complete object hash is identical before and after guard deletion
strict- and data-value-exact function sets have zero regressions
organicity improves only because the foreign include-guard finding disappears

patterns.rule: Treat every recovered-C library guard as a temporary authenticated exception, not permanent source shape. Re-run a one-variable deletion probe after include-graph changes; when the complete object hash and protected reports are unchanged, remove both the guard and its exception. Restore the exact source immediately if any text, relocation, or owned-data byte changes.
safe_actions: capture the candidate object hash before editing
delete only the guard override, not the natural header include
run one serialized owner rebuild
compare the complete object hash plus strict and data-value reports
remove the matching exception only after a byte-neutral result
record the successful owner pair as reusable evidence
examples: Last5 retained candidate object hash 13278cb14fc151b26a7c36b09096fc39967bcecc, 6/10 strict exact, and 6/10 data-value exact after `_MATH_H` was removed; organicity rose from 83 to 97.
Mgcall retained candidate object hash bb0ec516c3849bd52e38814bcc6ed63190de973e, 22/38 strict exact, and 22/38 data-value exact after `_MATH_H` was removed; organicity rose from 81 to 95.
Capevent retained candidate object hash d0d0cb678eb7b53e313957f1d63dee1cd197ad29, 172/237 strict exact, and 192/237 data-value exact after `_MATH_H` was removed.

Coin retained candidate object SHA-256 a1a3e91718666154b0b019a101494aa7c4b0cdd9fbcb8c06607be5e71217c0a3, 27/52 strict exact, and 33/52 data-value exact after `_MATH_H` was removed; organicity rose from 86 to 100.
counterexamples: If deletion restores target-absent weak constants or changes a visible math declaration, the exception is still active and must be retained with its existing evidence.
Do not generalize byte neutrality across owners; each translation unit has an independent include closure.
Do not replace the guard with another macro, pragma, or declaration-suppression trick.

patterns.title: Use the float absolute intrinsic when retail remains single-precision
patterns.summary: Under the MP6 GC/2.6 profile, a float expression passed through `fabs` can be promoted to double, producing `lfd`, `fmul`, `frsp`, 8-byte constants, extra saved FPR lifetimes, and shifted later `.sdata2` identities. When retail instead uses single-precision absolute arithmetic, `__fabsf` preserves the target `lfs`/`fmuls` shape and float-pool chronology. Four such corrections in Coin removed the two source-only double constants and made six previously value-exact functions strict exact without changing their bodies.
patterns.conditions: Apply as a GC/2.6 diagnostic only when the argument and result are authenticated floats and retail instructions prove single-precision absolute arithmetic. Do not replace an intentional double-precision `fabs` path.

source_condition.change: Replace `fabs` with `__fabsf` at an authenticated float-only expression whose target uses single-precision absolute arithmetic.
requires: the pinned GC/2.6 owner command and declaration visibility
float-typed inputs and consumers
target `fabs` with `lfs` or `fmuls` rather than a double load or multiply
before-and-after text, constant-pool, relocation, and exact-function comparison
a zero-regression check for every independently exact function in the owner

possible_changes: remove source-only 8-byte double constants
replace `lfd`/`fmul`/`frsp` with target `lfs`/`fmuls` arithmetic
reduce stack or saved-FPR pressure in the changed function
restore later `.sdata2` symbol and relocation chronology
convert downstream value-exact functions to strict exact without changing their instructions
known_signatures: candidate loads a double constant for a source literal suffixed with `f` while retail loads a float
candidate saves extra floating-point registers around an otherwise float-only expression
several unchanged functions are value exact but differ only in later small-data relocation identities
removing the promoted constants causes the later source pool order to align with retail

patterns.rule: When retail proves a float-only absolute expression, use the project-visible float intrinsic spelling that preserves single precision; verify that the promoted double constants disappear and that all affected text and relocation identities improve together.
safe_actions: compare the target and candidate arithmetic width before changing the call
look for exact same-game `__fabsf` precedent under the same include closure
change only the authenticated float absolute sites in one owner
compile one isolated object and compare strict plus data-value reports
retain the change only when the causal function and downstream pool consumers have zero exact regressions
examples: In main:board/coin, three 300.0f bounds and one 90.0f angle expression used `fabs`; changing only those four calls to `__fabsf` removed source-only double 300 and 90 pool entries.

The Coin correction raised strict exactness from 27/52 to 33/52 and added 2,900 strict-exact text bytes with no regression: CoinEffHook, mbCoinDispCreate, CoinDispOn, CoinDispMain, CoinDispOff, and mbCoinAddAllProcExecV.
Exact same-game Dice source uses `__fabsf` for the corresponding 90.0f ratio expression and emits the retail single-precision shape.
counterexamples: Keep `fabs` when retail intentionally loads or computes a double and the source-visible types authenticate double precision.
A value-equal float pool is not sufficient evidence; require target arithmetic width and relocation proof.
Do not introduce a local prototype, cast ladder, pragma, or synthetic constant merely to force the float intrinsic shape.

patterns.title: Classify linker-folded MWCC csects as compiled-unpaired until linked replay
patterns.summary: An MWCC source object may emit functions into named code csects that the split retail object presents as one `.text` section. Objdiff then leaves those same-named compiled functions unpaired even though they exist in the current object. This is a section-mapping limitation, not evidence of stale or missing source. In w01Dll, 20 helpers occupied `.text.common` plus `.text.after_common`; their 9,120 bytes completed the source code-section sum exactly, and the custom link reproduced the retail REL and full 137-file checksum.
patterns.conditions: Apply only when a target function has no objdiff pair, the current compiled object contains a same-named function, named source code csects are present, section sizes and order explain the complete target extent, relocation counts agree, and the owner linker script intentionally folds those csects into the target output. A same-named symbol alone is not exactness proof.

source_condition.change: Interpret an objdiff object gap for a source definition emitted into a non-default MWCC code csect.
requires: the freshly compiled source object
the split target object
same-named compiled function evidence
all target and source code-section sizes and order
target and source relocation counts
the generated owner linker script or authenticated selector configuration
serialized linked owner replay and retail checksum

possible_changes: objdiff target functions remain unpaired despite existing in the current source object
source `.text` is shorter while named code csects exactly supply the difference
compiled function order agrees after concatenating code csects
the linked REL is byte-identical even though the raw object report is not 100 percent paired
known_signatures: w01 target `.text` 0x164A8 versus source `.text` 0x14108 plus `.text.common` 0x2344 plus `.text.after_common` 0x5C
the two auxiliary csects total 0x23A0, exactly the 9,120 bytes objdiff left unpaired
target and source world01 objects both contain 5,673 relocations
serialized w01 REL SHA-1 196d7075abbe6eec3031c9484d25216de9dc0889 and full checksum 137 files OK

patterns.rule: If the current object contains a same-named function that objdiff cannot pair because it lives in an auxiliary code csect, classify it as compiled-unpaired rather than pending-build or missing-definition. Do not count it exact from object evidence alone; verify csect concatenation, relocation parity, linker selectors, the linked owner, and retail checksum.
safe_actions: list every code section and its size in both objects with the pinned DTK
confirm the current object contains each unpaired function by stable name and expected size
compare aggregate code size, section chronology, and relocation count
inspect the generated owner linker script for explicit csect placement
run one serialized linked REL replay and the project checksum before closing the owner
examples: w01Dll's 18 curve helpers occupy `.text.common` and its two timer helpers occupy `.text.after_common`; objdiff pairs the ordinary `.text` functions but cannot directly pair these auxiliary sections against the split target's single `.text`.
The updated recovery reporter records this case as 20 compiled-unpaired functions / 9,120 bytes and zero source-pending-build functions, then directs the owner to serialized linked replay.
counterexamples: Do not use this rule when the same-named function is absent from the freshly compiled object; that remains pending-build or missing-definition evidence.
Equal aggregate section size without function boundaries, relocation parity, and linker placement is not exactness proof.
A linked checksum cannot excuse invented padding, byte injection, synthetic csects, or unauthenticated linker controls.
Do not flatten authenticated source pragmas merely to make the raw object layout resemble the split retail object.

patterns.title: Rank target-first owner packets before widening recovery scope
patterns.summary: A useful first recovery packet is the smallest target-defined routine cluster whose sizes, relocations, calls, fields, globals, and prototypes are already authenticated. Ranking missing static routines by target extent and dependency inventory keeps unknown semantics out of the first probe; donor assembly or unknown bodies remain evidence, not source ownership.
patterns.conditions: Apply when an owner has missing static routines or a seam ledger but the target symbol, relocation, and caller inventory can be bounded. Re-rank only when target evidence or a verified consumer changes.

source_condition.change: Select the next target-first recovery packet instead of broadening a source stub or importing an unverified donor body.
requires: target function size and boundary inventory
target relocation and call inventory
authenticated fields, globals, prototypes, and consumer contracts for every packet item
a dependency-closed packet with no unresolved semantic field or ownership assumption
a caller, function-order, object, and linked-owner verification plan

possible_changes: smaller unknown-free recovery packets
ranked missing static routines by target bytes and dependency closure
fewer speculative donor-body or field imports
earlier detection of caller, ordering, relocation, or link-gate regressions
known_signatures: the target symbol table contains a sized static routine absent from the current source definition inventory
the routine's target calls and relocations are known while its source semantics are not
a donor assembly body would require inventing a field, global, prototype, or owner
a candidate function is exact in isolation but a caller or final owner gate remains unresolved

patterns.rule: Start with the smallest target-defined, dependency-closed packet whose fields, globals, prototypes, sizes, calls, and relocations are all authenticated. Use donor assembly and unknown bodies only as evidence. Function-level proof never waives caller, source-order, relocation, linked-owner, or final retail gates.
safe_actions: rank missing routines by target size, relocation count, and call/dependency inventory
reject a packet when any required field, global, prototype, or owner is still guessed
record donor assembly as a constraint and recover a natural source form independently
verify the packet's callers and neighboring order before widening its source scope
replay object, relocation, linked-owner, and retail gates before marking the packet complete
examples: The Config PauseCursor packet can be bounded from target symbols, source declarations, and authenticated cursor work fields before probing an unknown helper.
The Player mbPlayerMoveMain audit uses target size and lifetime evidence while keeping caller and final-order checks open.
counterexamples: A same-sized donor assembly body is not source ownership when its field or global accesses are unknown.
An exact isolated function does not prove its caller ABI, neighboring definition order, relocation ownership, or linked placement.
Do not widen a packet merely because a seam ledger names a routine; require target and consumer evidence first.

patterns.title: Treat a local declaration reorder as a one-probe stack-slot diagnostic
patterns.summary: Under the authenticated MWCC O0 profile, changing local declaration order can recolor saved registers or stack slots while leaving assignment and call evaluation order unchanged. A concrete target/candidate stack-offset swap with exact-size aligned control flow is useful layout evidence, but it does not prove original declaration chronology or justify a broad source reorder.
patterns.conditions: Apply only when Objdiff shows exact-size aligned control flow and the residual is a concrete stack-offset or register-color swap attributable to local lifetime order. Run one narrowly scoped probe and roll it back immediately if any broader text, relocation, pool, caller, or neighbor change appears.

source_condition.change: Reorder one authenticated local declaration or first-use boundary to test a stack-slot/register-color mismatch.
requires: pinned GC/2.6 compiler and translation-unit visibility
exact-size target/candidate control-flow alignment
a concrete target-versus-candidate stack offset or saved-register swap
authenticated local types and consumer lifetimes
before-and-after function, relocation, pool, caller, and neighboring-order checks

possible_changes: saved-register colors or stack offsets rotate
local loads and stores retain target evaluation order
a one-function residual closes without changing control flow
an over-broad declaration move changes unrelated functions, pools, or callers
known_signatures: Objdiff reports exact function size and aligned branches while only local stack offsets differ
the same assignments and calls remain in target order after the probe
a single declaration/first-use change swaps the observed local slot without new literals or relocations
moving a declaration changes neighboring functions or pool chronology, indicating the probe was too broad

patterns.rule: Use a local declaration-order change only as a single, reversible probe for a target-proven stack-slot or register-color swap. Keep assignment and call evaluation order intact, require immediate zero-regression evidence, and treat the observed symbol or slot order as emitted-layout evidence rather than proof of the original source order.
safe_actions: record the exact target and candidate stack offsets or register colors before editing
change one local declaration or first-use boundary in the owning function
compare strict function bytes, CFG alignment, relocations, local pools, callers, and neighboring order
retain the probe only when the concrete swap improves without broader change
roll back immediately when a second function, pool, relocation, or caller changes
examples: The Player mbPlayerMoveMain audit distinguishes a local lifetime/slot experiment from a broad helper or caller rewrite.
The Config PauseCursor packet is a bounded local-order diagnostic only when target offsets and exact CFG shape identify the affected locals.
counterexamples: A symbol-order difference without a concrete stack/register swap cannot authenticate declaration chronology.
Do not reorder locals to repair a pool or section difference when text, relocations, or consumers are not exact.
A probe that changes a caller, neighboring function, or literal pool is not a narrow local-order repair.

patterns.title: Use weak-order symbol differences as diagnostics, not source proof
patterns.summary: Normalized function, data, and local-pool order differences identify emitted-object facts: missing or extra names and relative inversions. They can prioritize target-first investigation, but they cannot authenticate a source declaration order, semantic owner, field meaning, or source reorder in isolation.
patterns.conditions: Apply when comparing two objects built under a pinned, comparable compiler/linker profile and when readelf symbol rows are available for both inputs. Treat generated local-pool identities as normalized diagnostics, not stable source names.

source_condition.change: Use a weak-order diff to select or reject a narrowly scoped source-order hypothesis.
requires: explicit target and source ELF/object paths
pinned readelf output or a safe readelf PATH resolution
normalized function, data, and local-pool sequences
target instruction, relocation, consumer, and owner-order evidence before any source move

possible_changes: function/data/local-pool sequence differences become reviewable
missing and extra normalized names identify inventory gaps
relative order inversions identify an emitted chronology mismatch
compiler-local pool numbering is collapsed without claiming semantic identity
known_signatures: the same normalized names occur in a different relative order
the target contains a name absent from the source or vice versa
multiple compiler-local @N pool symbols normalize to @
the report has an order inversion while text or relocation equivalence remains unproven

patterns.rule: Use weak-order output to describe and rank emitted layout evidence. Do not infer original declaration chronology, semantic ownership, compiler intent, or a justified source reorder from missing/extra names or inversions alone; require target instructions, relocations, consumers, and linked-owner gates.
safe_actions: pin both input paths and the readelf executable in the report
review normalized sequences together with target section, instruction, and relocation evidence
use an inversion to choose one falsifiable source hypothesis at a time
record rejected moves and counterexamples when text, pool, or consumer evidence regresses
close a source-order change only after object, caller, linked-owner, and retail verification
examples: tools/weak_order_diff.py reports normalized target/source functions, data, local pools, missing/extra names, and pairwise inversions without invoking ninja or editing source.
A local-pool @N versus lbl_* difference can prioritize relocation-ownership review while remaining unresolved source provenance.
counterexamples: A matching function list does not prove instruction bytes, relocation targets, callers, or final link placement.
A symbol inversion can be caused by csect/linker chronology or compiler-local naming and is not by itself a declaration-order proof.
Repeated normalized @ values describe sequence and multiplicity only; they do not identify which target pool row maps to which source row.
Do not add padding, pragmas, synthetic constants, or donor definitions solely to make the report order match.

patterns.title: Retain a natural semantic barrier when authenticated inline asm owns the target shape
patterns.summary: An authenticated same-game PauseCursorPosNextSet donor uses register pointers and inline psq_l/lfs/psq_st/stfs operations; the retail target saves f28-f31 with frame size 0x90. Natural direct HuVecF copy reached 700/724 bytes at 88.607735%, while a typed pointer copy reached 90.756905% but remained 700/724 with frame size 0x70. Legal C controls therefore cannot create the inline-assembly clobber and save set, which is an explicit exactness barrier rather than a source-reordering invitation.
patterns.conditions: Apply only when provenance authenticates the retail inline-assembly boundary and project policy forbids inline asm, register shaping, or equivalent forced code generation. Keep the barrier scoped to the affected owner and target operation.

source_condition.change: Choose the natural semantic C form for an authenticated vector transfer whose retail register pressure is owned by inline assembly.
requires: same-game donor or retained source evidence for register-pointer plus psq_l/lfs/psq_st/stfs assembly
target frame and saved-FPR evidence
strict function-size and instruction reports for natural direct and typed-pointer controls
project policy ruling out inline asm, explicit register variables, and forced FPR pressure
caller, relocation, pool, and linked-owner review before closing the residual

possible_changes: natural aggregate C emits a smaller or different frame and saved-register set
typed pointer mediation can improve nearby instructions without creating the target clobber/save set
target-only f28-f31 saves and frame 0x90 remain unmatched
the owner remains honestly nonexact with a recorded mechanism barrier
known_signatures: target contains inline displacement psq_l/lfs/psq_st/stfs islands and no helper call
target saves f28-f31 at frame 0x90 while natural direct HuVecF remains frame 0x70
direct HuVecF copy measures 700/724 at 88.607735%
typed pointer copy measures 700/724 at 90.756905% but does not create the target save set

patterns.rule: When provenance proves that retail register pressure and vector transfer shape belong to inline assembly that project policy forbids, retain the clean natural semantic C form, record an explicit exactness barrier, and do not fabricate FPR pressure, register variables, asm scaffolds, or a matching claim.
safe_actions: record the donor provenance, target frame, saved FPRs, and exact probe scores
keep direct semantic HuVecF or typed-pointer controls as measured diagnostics only
compare callers, relocations, local pools, and neighboring order before accepting any collateral improvement
mark the owner nonexact with the mechanism barrier and preserve the rejected controls
reopen only if an authenticated project-policy-compatible source boundary explains the same save set
examples: PauseCursorPosNextSet retains target f28-f31/frame0x90 pressure while direct HuVecF and typed-pointer controls remain 700/724; the gap is recorded instead of forced with asm or register shaping.
The same-game vector-copy audit treats a displacement psq_l/lfs/psq_st/stfs island as a mechanism boundary, not evidence for invented source fields or declaration order.
counterexamples: A natural C function that reaches exact text and relocations without asm is not subject to this barrier.
A higher percentage from typed pointers is not a match when frame size, saved FPRs, or relocation ownership remain wrong.
Do not generalize a donor's inline assembly to unrelated owners or claim that an asm scaffold was original source.
